title: -ir and -re verbs, and the partitive
summary: Conjugate finir, vendre, prendre and boire, and say 'some' with du, de la, de l' and des.
focus: Regular -ir and -re verbs, prendre and boire, and the partitive article
content:
## -ir and -re verbs: finir, vendre

Two more families of regular verbs. Regular **-ir** verbs like **finir** (to finish) and **choisir** (to choose) add **-iss-** in the plural. Regular **-re** verbs like **vendre** (to sell) and **attendre** (to wait for) drop **-re**; the **il** form has no ending at all.

| | finir | vendre |
|---|---|---|
| je | finis | vends |
| tu | finis | vends |
| il / elle / on | finit | vend |
| nous | finissons | vendons |
| vous | finissez | vendez |
| ils / elles | finissent | vendent |

The three singular forms sound the same, and the final **d** of **il vend** is silent. **Attendre** needs no word for "for": **j'attends le bus** (I'm waiting for the bus).

## Prendre and boire

Two everyday irregular verbs for eating and drinking. **Prendre** (to take; to have food or drink) drops its **d** in the plural and doubles the **n** in **ils prennent**. **Boire** (to drink) switches to **buv-** for nous and vous and **boiv-** for ils.

| | prendre | boire |
|---|---|---|
| je | prends | bois |
| tu | prends | bois |
| il / elle / on | prend | boit |
| nous | prenons | buvons |
| vous | prenez | buvez |
| ils / elles | prennent | boivent |

- **Je prends du pain.** (I'm having some bread.)
- **Nous buvons de l'eau.** (We drink water.)

## The partitive: du, de la, de l', des

For an amount of food or drink you don't count ("some", often unsaid in English), French uses **de** + the article:

| | partitive | example |
|---|---|---|
| masculine | **du** | du fromage |
| feminine | **de la** | de la soupe |
| before a vowel | **de l'** | de l'eau |
| plural | **des** | des légumes |

After a negation, all of them become **de** (**d'** before a vowel): **je ne mange pas de viande**, **il ne boit pas d'eau**. Likes and dislikes keep **le / la / les**: **j'aime le fromage**, but **je prends du fromage**.

quiz.prompt: Nous ___ nos devoirs avant le dîner.
quiz.explanation: Regular -ir verbs add -iss- in the plural: nous finissons. 'Finissez' is the vous form.
hints: Nous takes -ons, and -ir verbs add -iss- before it.

quiz.prompt: Complete with finir: Les enfants ___ leurs pâtes.
quiz.explanation: Ils / elles of finir: finissent. The -ent is silent; you hear the -iss-.

quiz.prompt: Complete with vendre: Vous ___ du fromage ?
quiz.explanation: Vendre drops -re and adds -ez for vous: vous vendez.
The il / elle form of a regular -re verb has no ending: il vend. 'Vends' is je / tu, 'vendent' is ils.

quiz.prompt: Complete with prendre: Ce soir, ils ___ du poisson.
quiz.explanation: Prendre is irregular: ils prennent, with a double n.
hints: Ils form of prendre: double n.

quiz.explanation: Lait is masculine and uncounted: du lait.

quiz.prompt: Complete with du, de la, de l' or des: Elle mange ___ soupe.
quiz.explanation: Soupe is feminine and uncounted: de la soupe.

quiz.prompt: 'Je ne mange pas de la viande.' is correct French.
quiz.explanation: After a negation the partitive becomes de: je ne mange pas de viande.
hints: What happens to du / de la / des after ne … pas?

quiz.prompt: 'Vous buvez de l'eau ?' is correct French.
quiz.explanation: Boire uses the stem buv- for nous and vous (vous buvez), and eau starts with a vowel: de l'eau.
hints: Check the vous form of boire.

conversations.title: At the corner shop
conversations.scenario: Camille does her shopping at Monsieur Durand's little grocery shop.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Bonjour monsieur ! Vous vendez du fromage ?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Bonjour madame. Oui, nous vendons du fromage et du lait.
lines.meaning: Hello. Yes, we sell cheese and milk.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Parfait. Je prends du fromage de chèvre, s'il vous plaît.
lines.meaning: Perfect. I'll have some goat's cheese, please.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Voilà. Vous prenez aussi du pain ?
lines.meaning: Here you are. Are you taking some bread too?

lines.text: Non merci, je n'achète pas de pain aujourd'hui.
lines.meaning: No thanks, I'm not buying bread today.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Et de la confiture ? Elle est très bonne.
lines.meaning: And some jam? It's very good.

lines.text: Oui, je choisis la confiture de fraises.
lines.meaning: Yes, I'll choose the strawberry jam.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Très bien. Vous voulez aussi de l'eau ?
lines.meaning: Very good. Would you like some water too?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Oui, une bouteille. Mes enfants boivent beaucoup d'eau.
lines.meaning: Yes, a bottle. My children drink a lot of water.

concept.title: Prendre at the café
concept.markdown: In a café or restaurant, **je prends** means "I'll have": **Je prends un croissant.** The same verb hides inside **apprendre** (to learn) and **comprendre** (to understand), with the same forms: **je comprends, nous comprenons, ils comprennent**.

guide.tip: Ask: some of it (du / de la / de l' / des), or the thing in general, as in liking it (le / la / les)?

bites.title: -ir: add -iss-
bites.rule: Regular -ir verbs (finir, choisir): je finis, tu finis, il finit, nous finissons, vous finissez, ils finissent. The plural adds -iss-.

bites.title: -re: nothing for il
bites.rule: Regular -re verbs (vendre, attendre): drop -re, add -s, -s, nothing, -ons, -ez, -ent. Il vend, il attend.

bites.title: Prendre and boire
bites.rule: Irregular: je prends, nous prenons, ils prennent; je bois, nous buvons, ils boivent.
bites.example: Je prends du pain et je bois du lait.
bites.example_meaning: I have bread and I drink milk.

bites.title: Some = du, de la, de l', des
bites.rule: Uncounted food and drink takes the partitive. After ne … pas it becomes de: pas de pain, pas d'eau.
bites.example: Je mange du fromage, mais pas de viande.
bites.example_meaning: I eat cheese, but not meat.

sorts.title: du, de la, de l' or des?
sorts.why: Masculine du, feminine de la, de l' before a vowel, des for plurals.

sorts.title: Which family?
sorts.why: Finir, choisir and réussir add -iss- in the plural; vendre, attendre and répondre follow -s -s - -ons -ez -ent; prendre and boire change their stems.

spots.sentence: Nous finons le repas à midi.
spots.why: Regular -ir verbs add -iss- in the plural: nous finissons.

spots.sentence: Je ne bois pas du café.
spots.why: After a negation the partitive becomes de: pas de café.
Prendre is irregular: ils prennent, with a double n.
Boire uses buv- for nous and vous: vous buvez.

builds.text: Nous finissons le repas à midi.
builds.meaning: We finish the meal at noon.

builds.text: Je ne mange pas de viande.
Ils prennent du pain et du fromage.

## Manger et boire à Eldmark

At **la taverne du Dragon Vert**, the innkeeper **vend du ragoût, de la viande et de l'hydromel**. The dwarves **boivent de l'hydromel**; Nym the elf **ne boit pas d'hydromel**, with **de** after a negation. Borin **prend du fromage**, and the guild **finit** its quest.

vocabulary.example: La guilde finit la quête avant la nuit.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The guild finishes the quest before nightfall.

vocabulary.example_meaning: The innkeeper sells bread and cheese.

vocabulary.example_meaning: Borin has some meat and some stew.

vocabulary.example_meaning: The dwarves drink mead at the tavern.

vocabulary.example_meaning: The mage Séla eats black bread.

vocabulary.example_meaning: Nym the elf drinks water from the river.

vocabulary.example_meaning: We drink mead after the quest.

vocabulary.example_meaning: I'll have some stew, please.

meadowbrook.content:
## Au marché de Meadowbrook

At the market, Nora **vend des fraises, du maïs et de la confiture**, and Rosa **choisit des citrouilles**. Léo **prend du poisson** for dinner; the cows **boivent de l'eau** at the river. In winter **il n'y a pas de fraises**, with **de** after the negation.

vocabulary.example: Nora vend des fraises au marché.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Nora sells strawberries at the market.

vocabulary.example: Je prends du lait frais à la ferme.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I get fresh milk at the farm.

rustwake.content:
## Manger et boire à Rustwake

Outside **le Dôme**, Marta **vend de l'eau filtrée et du soda Saphir** for nuts. You **prends du tonique** after the storm, the scavengers **boivent de l'eau**, and the robot gardener **ne boit pas d'eau**, with **de** after a negation.

vocabulary.example_meaning: Marta sells filtered water for nuts.

vocabulary.example: Je prends du tonique après la tempête de cendres.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I take some tonic after the ash storm.

vocabulary.example: Le chien de garde boit de l'eau filtrée.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The guard dog drinks filtered water.

vocabulary.example: Les fouilleurs finissent leur exploration le soir.
